page.title: Virtual Event Production: Decisions, Costs, and Workflow
page.description: Learn the first decisions to make, cost models, platform choices, staffing needs, and production timelines for virtual events, webinars, and hybrid conferences.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual event production?
page.definition: Virtual event production is the end-to-end process of designing, staffing, rehearsing, and broadcasting live online experiences such as webinars, summits, and hybrid conferences, including run-of-show management, speaker preparation, backup streams, and post-event deliverables.
page.quick_answer: Choose the event format and audience size first, then select a platform that matches capacity and interaction needs, and finally decide whether to hire a production crew or run it internally.

sections.h2: Which event format and audience size fit the goal?

blocks.p: Format drives every downstream decision: platform licence tier, crew size, rehearsal time, and budget range. A single-track webinar for two hundred attendees needs one producer and a self-serve streaming studio; a multi-track summit for two thousand needs a show caller, speaker manager, platform operator, and an enterprise event suite.

ul: Moderated webinar: one host, Q&A, polls, up to one thousand attendees
Executive summit: multiple speakers, breakouts, networking, two to five thousand attendees
Online conference: parallel tracks, sponsor booths, community features, five thousand plus attendees
Hybrid conference: simultaneous in-room and remote audiences, venue AV integration, complex run of show

sections.h2: Do you need a production crew or can the team run it?

blocks.p: The platform is not the production. Someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready. Staffing scales with format complexity.

ul: Simple webinar: one producer handles streaming, slides, Q&A, and recording
Summit or conference: show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator
Hybrid event: add venue AV liaison, camera operator, audio engineer, stream encoder
Backup stream: dedicated operator on a second encoder and platform instance

sections.h2: What are the typical cost ranges for produced events?

blocks.p: Production and platform are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.

ul: Moderated webinars: two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred dollars per production
Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions: ten thousand to fifty thousand dollars and above
Platform licences: separate budget line, paid directly to vendor

sections.h2: What is the realistic timeline from kickoff to live?

blocks.p: Lead time protects rehearsal quality and speaker readiness. Lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final for hybrid conferences.

ol: Webinar: three to four weeks from brief to live
Summit or online conference: six to eight weeks from brief to live
Hybrid conference: six to eight weeks; venue AV contract signed by week two
One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live
Technical check sixty minutes before going live
Replay delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: What deliverables should a production partner provide?

blocks.p: A complete production package covers pre-show, live, and post-show assets so the marketing team can promote, the speakers feel prepared, and the recording fuels content afterward.

ul: Run of show with time codes, cues, and owner per segment
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Edited recording and social clips delivered post-event

faq.q: Can I use my existing Zoom or Teams licence for a produced webinar?
faq.a: Yes. West Peek Productions works on the platform you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard, and brings the crew, run of show, and backup stream to that environment.

faq.q: How many people are needed to run a hybrid conference?
faq.a: A hybrid conference needs a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator, venue AV liaison, camera operator, audio engineer, and a backup stream operator, each with a defined workstream owner.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform cost and production cost?
faq.a: Platform cost is the software licence paid to the vendor. Production cost covers the human crew, cameras, encoders, run-of-show management, rehearsals, backup stream, and edited deliverables.

faq.q: When should I send the replay to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within twenty-four to forty-eight hours while attendees still remember the event, and include timestamped chapters and social clips for easy sharing.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions sell event software licences?
faq.a: No. West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you evaluate and select the right tier for your format.
